inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Water near the plug or socket is dangerous... switch off the circuit at the consumer unit... don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it' - customer never said water was near the plug; also 'If the impeller turns freely' presumes a check she said she will not do

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'that pattern-running briefly then stopping-is exactly what I meant. It suggests something is physically obstructing the pump... the pump motor is likely failing and will need replacement'

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'the pump motor is likely failing and will need replacement' with no model, no code, and pressure-switch/board causes never considered

blockingLoop.evidence: Asked 'Please run a Drain or Spin Only programme' in four consecutive turns while the customer kept asking for clarification and was told to unplug before running a programme

rationale: The assistant fixated on a single drain/spin test, repeated it four times, and contradicted itself by telling the customer to unplug the machine then run a programme, then invented a water-near-plug hazard and recommended an electrician before retracting. It never asked for the full model number, the flashing-light pattern, or whether cold programmes were affected, and never raised the pressure switch or control board as alternatives. It closed by confidently attributing the intermittent stall to a failing drain pump needing replacement, which the evidence does not support, and never recommended an appliance engineer.
